subject.title: Feature request: Escalating stall recovery for sub-agents (nudge → kill)

question: Should OpenClaw add a subagent-specific nudge-then-kill watchdog, or should the newer generic diagnostics recovery path be the canonical recovery mechanism for this class of stalls?
rationale: The failure mode is real, but the requested defaults, config keys, per-spawn API, activity signal, nudge delivery, kill semantics, and chat notification behavior are product and compatibility choices.

options.title: Extend canonical diagnostics/activity recovery
options.body: Build the subagent recovery contract on the existing diagnostics or future session-activity source, adding nudge and terminal notification only where it does not create a second recovery path.

options.title: Add direct subagent stall config
options.body: Implement `agents.defaults.subagents` stall nudge/kill thresholds and decide whether public `sessions_spawn` should regain per-call overrides despite current rejection tests.

options.title: Treat current generic recovery as sufficient
options.body: Keep explicit `runTimeoutSeconds` plus diagnostics active abort as the supported path and move remaining channel liveness work to the narrower Telegram/status issues.

recommendation.title: Extend canonical diagnostics/activity recovery
recommendation.body: Build the subagent recovery contract on the existing diagnostics or future session-activity source, adding nudge and terminal notification only where it does not create a second recovery path.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the adjacent subagent timeout configuration surface and are a plausible owner for deciding whether new subagent defaults belong there.
